blueprint.name: BuilderAI
blueprint.vision: Build a trustworthy, model-independent software engineering platform grounded in durable project context.

goals.statement: Maintain one canonical machine-readable Project Brain per project.
successCriteria: Runtime consumers and project documentation reference the same validated state.

goals.statement: Keep project knowledge portable across tools and models.
successCriteria: The Project Brain core imports no AI, UI, storage-vendor, or network SDK.

goals.statement: Preserve project identity and append-only delivery history.
successCriteria: No supported command can rewrite identity, decisions, completed work, or completed sprints.

features.name: Project Blueprint
features.summary: Project vision, goals, features, requirements, constraints, stack references, and ownership.

features.name: Project Memory
features.summary: Completed and pending work, important decisions, and architectural rules.

features.name: Progress Log
features.summary: Current milestone, completed sprints, and completed task identifiers.

features.name: Task Engine
features.summary: Validated Todo, In Progress, Done, and Blocked task lifecycle.

features.name: Blueprint Reader
features.summary: Deterministic discovery, validation, analysis, consistency checking, and structured summaries for BuilderAI project documentation.

features.name: Context Builder
features.summary: Task-scoped selection, prioritization, dependency resolution, validation, and size-bounded packaging of project context.

features.name: AI Provider Adapter
features.summary: Provider-neutral capability, request, response, configuration, validation, compatibility, registry, and error contracts without an integration or execution workflow.

features.name: Prompt Orchestrator
features.summary: Deterministic transformation of a validated Context Package into one versioned, structured, ordered, deduplicated, and size-bounded Prompt Package.

features.name: Execution Engine
features.summary: Provider-neutral validation and deterministic lifecycle, retry, timeout, cancellation, and result orchestration without runtime execution.

features.name: OpenAI Responses Provider
features.summary: The first isolated AIProvider implementation, mapping one validated Prompt Package to one non-streaming OpenAI Responses API call and returning validated BuilderAI output.

features.name: Response Processor
features.summary: Provider-independent validation, normalization, manifest generation, and integrity verification that converts a completed provider exchange into one deterministic Response Package without side effects.

features.name: Project Change Planner
features.summary: Provider-independent transformation of a validated Response Package into one deterministic, conflict-checked, effect-free Project Change Plan.

features.name: Safe File Apply Engine
features.summary: Provider-independent two-phase validation, protected-path preflight, conditional filesystem application, and exact Apply Result reporting behind root-scoped ports.

features.name: Build and Verification Engine
features.summary: Provider- and framework-independent orchestration of project, dependency, build, and test verification through validated ports and one deterministic report.

features.name: Minimal BuilderAI UI
features.summary: Responsive dashboard and human-controlled project workspace that present canonical project state and existing workflow evidence through a typed UI orchestration port.

features.name: Google Gemini Provider
features.summary: An isolated Gemini API implementation of the existing AIProvider port for configuration-selected local development.

requirements.statement: Store mutable Project Brain state in one canonical machine-readable file.
acceptanceCriteria: The canonical file passes the production runtime parser in CI.
Project Brain policy documents do not repeat mutable state.

requirements.statement: Mutate Project Brain state only through explicit intent-based commands.
acceptanceCriteria: The application service API exposes no unrestricted aggregate replacement.
Project identity and append-only histories are enforced at the repository boundary.

requirements.statement: Validate every Project Brain snapshot before it enters storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid snapshots return path-specific validation issues.

requirements.statement: Discover required BuilderAI documents through a storage-independent port.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing, duplicate, and unknown documents are reported deterministically.

requirements.statement: Parse versioned documentation and produce a structured project summary without AI.
acceptanceCriteria: Required sections, versions, schema compatibility, relationships, conflicts, and duplicated mutable state are validated.
The summary contains overview, architecture, modules, features, milestone, work, risks, and missing documentation.

requirements.statement: Select only project information relevant to the current task using deterministic rules and explicit dependency relationships.
acceptanceCriteria: Context selection resolves related modules, documents, tasks, decisions, and source files without external services.
Context priority follows the approved governance-to-source order.

requirements.statement: Produce one validated, strongly typed Context Package within configurable limits.
acceptanceCriteria: Oversized, duplicate, conflicting, incomplete, and invalid context is rejected or deterministically omitted according to policy.
The Context Package remains framework-, storage-, and consumer-independent.

requirements.statement: Define one versioned provider port and validated request/response boundary without provider-specific dependencies or configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: The core contract imports no SDK, framework, storage, network, credential, environment, or provider implementation.
Requests accept only a validated Prompt Package; responses use typed artifacts, diagnostics, warnings, statistics, and character-based usage.

requirements.statement: Discover compatible registered providers deterministically without invoking provider behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Registration validates and snapshots provider identity, capabilities, and closed provider-neutral configuration.
Discovery accounts for enablement, priority, execution mode, timeout, context size, requested artifacts, and required capabilities.

requirements.statement: Transform one validated Context Package into one provider-neutral, versioned Prompt Package with stable sections and no duplicated information.
acceptanceCriteria: Identity, architecture, task, goals, constraints, context, instructions, expected output, and metadata have one structured section owner.
Future provider requests accept the Prompt Package instead of raw Context Package and duplicate task state.

requirements.statement: Select validated prompt template versions deterministically and enforce exact serialized prompt budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: Templates reject unsupported versions, duplicate identity/version pairs, missing sections, and unstable ordering.
Optional section omissions are recorded, while mandatory prompt content is never truncated.

requirements.statement: Coordinate each validated Prompt Package through one explicit, append-only execution lifecycle without invoking a provider.
acceptanceCriteria: Only legal versioned state transitions can change an execution snapshot.
Execution identity, revision, attempt count, timestamps, and transition history remain consistent and validated.

requirements.statement: Represent retry, timeout, priority, validation, failure, cancellation, and terminal result policy as closed provider-neutral contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Retry and timeout services return deterministic decisions and perform no waiting, scheduling, cancellation, provider, tool, or network behavior.
Versioned results accept only terminal snapshots and contain validated diagnostics, timing, usage, artifact placeholders, errors, and metadata.

requirements.statement: Integrate exactly one OpenAI Responses provider without changing provider-neutral core contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: The official SDK, credentials, wire contracts, and provider errors remain isolated under src/providers/openai.
Every request and response crosses existing validated Prompt Package, AIProvider, and Execution Engine boundaries.
The adapter performs one non-streaming call with SDK retries disabled and exposes no tools, files, images, history, persistence, or telemetry.

requirements.statement: Transform one validated completed provider response and its correlated Execution Result into one versioned deterministic Response Package.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated artifacts, diagnostics, warnings, and scalar metadata are normalized and ordered deterministically.
Only Source File, Documentation, Configuration, Test, and Patch artifacts are accepted, and processing performs no filesystem, Git, network, persistence, telemetry, or execution effect.

requirements.statement: Produce and verify a deterministic artifact manifest before response output crosses the processing boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Each manifest entry records a normalized safe logical path, closed artifact type, checksum, UTF-8 byte size, and validated metadata.
Duplicate paths, unsupported types, malformed metadata, oversized content, checksum mismatches, and cross-contract identity or artifact drift are rejected with typed path-specific issues.

requirements.statement: Transform one validated Response Package into one versioned deterministic Project Change Plan without inspecting or modifying project state.
acceptanceCriteria: Every operation has explicit Create File, Update File, or Delete File intent and preserves source artifact and execution references.

The plan contains a deterministic change set, exact summary, structured risks, warnings, and scalar metadata while performing no filesystem, Git, network, build, test, rollback, persistence, or project-modification effect.

requirements.statement: Reject ambiguous, unsupported, duplicated, conflicting, unsafe, or incorrectly ordered project change intents before a plan crosses the boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Case-insensitive path aliases, duplicate operation identities, conflicting operation kinds, file/tree conflicts, patch semantics, invalid metadata, summary drift, and broken source references fail with typed path-specific issues.
Operations use canonical create, update, delete, and logical-path order and every plan records that current project-state preconditions remain unverified.

requirements.statement: Apply only validated Project Change Plans through root-scoped filesystem and clock ports using closed conditional Create File, Update File, and Delete File operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Core orchestration imports no filesystem implementation, provider, framework, Git, process, network, build, test, deployment, telemetry, or rollback capability.
Every result records actual created, updated, deleted, and skipped files, warnings, stable errors, non-negative duration, and defensive scalar metadata.

requirements.statement: Complete all plan, protected-path, target, parent, entry-kind, and inspection validation before the first filesystem mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid plans, protected paths, missing or wrong-kind targets, invalid parents, symlinks, operation-limit violations, and inspection failures cause zero filesystem changes.

Filesystem methods enforce conditional create-if-absent, update-if-regular-file, and delete-if-regular-file semantics after preflight; execution stops on first mutation failure and honestly reports Failed or Partially Applied without rollback.

requirements.statement: Verify only successful File Apply Results through a fixed Project, Dependency, Build, and Test pipeline whose external behavior exists behind explicit ports.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid or non-Applied inputs invoke zero verification ports, while accepted inputs execute every stage once in canonical order.
Thrown or malformed port results become safe failed stage evidence without leaking implementation details or suppressing later stages.

requirements.statement: Produce one versioned deterministic Verification Report whose overall status, stage evidence, findings, duration, and metadata are runtime validated.
acceptanceCriteria: Overall status is Passed when all stages pass, Failed when no stage passes, and Partially Passed for mixed outcomes.
Stage order, result consistency, flattened findings, bounded metadata, duplicate findings, configuration, and report structure reject drift with typed validation issues.

requirements.statement: Present canonical project status and the existing request, response, plan, approval, apply, and verification workflow through an accessible responsive dashboard and project workspace.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard project facts are loaded through the production canonical Project Brain parser rather than duplicated in UI source.
The workspace provides project context, request input, conversation updates, deterministic progress, explicit approval, and readable typed evidence panels.

requirements.statement: Keep the browser UI dependent on a typed workflow port and fail closed when no authorized server runtime composition exists.
acceptanceCriteria: UI modules import existing core contracts as types and do not change, duplicate, or bypass core validation and business policy.
The shipped workspace exposes no provider credential, filesystem, process, Git, deployment, repair, authentication, billing, collaboration, or provider-selection implementation.

requirements.statement: Select exactly one supported local AI provider through server configuration without changing core contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenAI and Gemini implement the same unchanged AIProvider port.
Only the selected provider credentials and model are required, and no provider secret enters browser code.

constraints.rationale: The permanent context foundation must be trustworthy before product AI is considered.

constraints.statement: Do not select or introduce durable persistence in Sprint 1.
constraints.rationale: Storage requirements and operational constraints are not approved.

constraints.statement: Do not begin Sprint 2 without explicit stakeholder approval.
constraints.rationale: Sprint boundaries control scope and architectural risk.

constraints.statement: Do not implement AI, LLM, chat, code-generation, automation, deployment, or API calls in Sprint 2.
constraints.rationale: The Blueprint Reader is limited to deterministic project understanding.

constraints.statement: Do not implement models, chat, code generation, API calls, deployment, or automation in Sprint 3.
constraints.rationale: The Context Builder is limited to deterministic, bounded preparation of project context.

constraints.statement: Do not implement provider integrations, prompt execution, code generation, chat, network requests, credentials, environment configuration, deployment, or automation in Sprint 4.
constraints.rationale: The AI Provider Adapter sprint is limited to provider-neutral contracts, validation, discovery, and compatibility policy.

constraints.statement: Do not implement provider integrations, prompt execution, AI execution, streaming, tool execution, network requests, HTTP, credentials, environment configuration, or provider syntax in Sprint 5.
constraints.rationale: Prompt Orchestration is limited to deterministic, provider-neutral Prompt Package construction and validation.

constraints.statement: Do not implement providers, model execution, HTTP, fetch, networking, credentials, SDK imports, tool execution, active cancellation, scheduling, waiting, or runtime timeout enforcement in Sprint 6.
constraints.rationale: The Execution Engine foundation is limited to pure provider-neutral lifecycle contracts, validation, and orchestration decisions.

constraints.statement: Sprint 7 integrates only the OpenAI Responses API and excludes routing, streaming, tools, functions, files, images, parallel or background execution, history, agents, UI, persistence, and telemetry.
constraints.rationale: The first integration must prove the existing architecture through the smallest controlled external boundary.

constraints.statement: Sprint 8 is limited to provider-independent, in-memory Response Package validation, normalization, manifest generation, and integrity verification without modifying a project.
constraints.rationale: Provider output must become deterministic and verifiable before any separately approved project-change capability may consume it.

constraints.statement: Sprint 9 is limited to provider-independent, effect-free Project Change Plan generation and excludes filesystem access, Git, automatic modification, build or test execution, rollback, UI, streaming, multi-provider work, and Sprint 10 capabilities.
constraints.rationale: Change intent must be explicit, deterministic, conflict-checked, and reviewable before any project effect can be considered.

constraints.statement: Sprint 10 is limited to provider-independent validated file application behind ports and excludes Git, rollback, build or test execution, deployment, networking, provider changes, UI, streaming, and Sprint 11 work.
constraints.rationale: The first project effect boundary must remain narrow, protected, preflight-atomic, deterministic, and honest about non-transactional failures.

constraints.statement: Sprint 11 is limited to provider- and framework-independent verification orchestration behind ports and excludes UI, provider changes, Git, rollback, deployment, automatic repair, networking, streaming, concrete runners, and Sprint 12 work.
constraints.rationale: Verification policy and evidence must be deterministic before process-capable adapters or subsequent workflow automation are separately approved.

constraints.statement: Sprint 12 is limited to a minimal responsive BuilderAI dashboard and project workspace over existing typed contracts and excludes core changes, live privileged runtime composition, authentication, billing, collaboration, provider selection, deployment, Git UI, automatic repair, and Sprint 13 work.
constraints.rationale: The first interface must make workflow evidence and approval understandable without weakening existing execution, filesystem, verification, or authorization boundaries.

architecturalRules.rule: Read and validate project-brain.json before changing code.
architecturalRules.rationale: All implementation must use the current canonical project context.

architecturalRules.rule: Mutate Project Brain state only through explicit intent-based commands.
architecturalRules.rationale: Generic replacement can bypass domain history and identity guarantees.

architecturalRules.rule: Decisions, completed work, and completed sprints are append-only.
Do not implement AI capabilities without a separately approved milestone.
architecturalRules.rationale: The Project Brain foundation does not authorize product AI.

architecturalRules.rule: Send a Prompt Package to an external provider only after the caller authorizes and classifies its content.
architecturalRules.rationale: A technically valid Prompt Package may still contain confidential source or project information.

architecturalRules.rule: Treat provider output as untrusted data until it has crossed the validated Response Package boundary; a Response Package never authorizes filesystem, Git, execution, persistence, or project mutation.
architecturalRules.rationale: Deterministic packaging and integrity evidence must remain separate from any future reviewed and authorized project-change workflow.

architecturalRules.rule: Project change intent must cross the validated Project Change Plan boundary before review; a plan never authorizes filesystem, Git, build, test, rollback, persistence, or project-modification effects.
architecturalRules.rationale: Planning must remain deterministic, conflict-aware review evidence and cannot substitute for current-state verification or explicit execution authorization.

architecturalRules.rule: Authorized file effects must pass through the Safe File Apply Engine, mandatory protected-path policy, complete preflight, and root-scoped conditional filesystem port; partial application must never be reported as atomic success.
architecturalRules.rationale: A single narrow effect boundary prevents validation bypass, unrestricted filesystem access, protected-path changes, symlink traversal, and misleading multi-file outcomes.

architecturalRules.rule: Project, dependency, build, and test verification may occur only after an Applied File Apply Result and only through the fixed Verification Engine pipeline and validated ports; a Verification Report never authorizes repair, Git, rollback, deployment, or another sprint.
architecturalRules.rationale: A single evidence boundary keeps execution implementations outside core, prevents stage omission and status drift, and does not turn verification into open-ended automation.

architecturalRules.rule: The browser interface may present and request existing workflow behavior only through its typed orchestration port; absent an authorized server composition it must remain visibly disconnected and perform no provider, filesystem, process, Git, deployment, or repair effect.
architecturalRules.rationale: A presentation boundary must not become a privileged runtime bypass or fabricate successful project evidence.

architecturalRules.rule: Live MVP effects are allowed only in the explicitly configured same-origin loopback profile, against the server-held validated plan, after human acknowledgement, through root-scoped conditional filesystem and bounded verification adapters; all remote, shared, multi-instance, and untrusted-project use remains prohibited.
architecturalRules.rationale: The v1.0 composition must not turn a local integration milestone into an unauthenticated hosted execution service or let browser data become effect authority.

decisionLog.title: Make the Project Brain the project authority
decisionLog.context: Future engineering tools require durable context independent of chat history.
decisionLog.decision: All changes begin by reading the canonical Project Brain and its policy documents.
decisionLog.rationale: Repository-owned context is portable and reviewable.
alternatives: Tool-specific conversational memory

positive: Portable project context
negative: Project state must be maintained deliberately

decisionLog.title: Isolate a model-independent core
decisionLog.context: BuilderAI may use different interfaces and infrastructure over time.
decisionLog.decision: Keep Project Brain policy free of UI, AI-provider, network, and storage-vendor dependencies.
decisionLog.rationale: Domain policy must remain portable.
alternatives: Place policy in Next.js routes

positive: Independent domain testing
negative: Explicit boundaries require maintenance

decisionLog.title: Use dependency-free runtime validation
decisionLog.context: Runtime input requires validation without expanding the dependency surface.
decisionLog.decision: Use internal validators for schema version 1.
decisionLog.rationale: The current schema is small enough to maintain locally.
alternatives: Add a schema-validation dependency

positive: No new runtime dependency
negative: Validation code requires disciplined tests

decisionLog.title: Use optimistic repository revisions
decisionLog.context: Concurrent updates must not silently overwrite one another.
decisionLog.decision: Require an expected revision for every Project Brain commit.
decisionLog.rationale: Compare-and-save exposes conflicts explicitly.
alternatives: Last-write-wins updates

positive: Lost updates are rejected
negative: Callers must handle revision conflicts

decisionLog.title: Use explicit task transitions
decisionLog.context: Implicit status assignment makes delivery state unreliable.
decisionLog.decision: Enforce documented task transitions, blockers, and dependencies.
decisionLog.rationale: Task progress must remain auditable.
alternatives: Allow unrestricted status assignment

positive: Consistent task state
negative: Corrections require explicit reopening

decisionLog.title: Use one canonical machine-readable Project Brain
decisionLog.context: Markdown and runtime fixtures duplicated mutable state and could drift.
decisionLog.decision: Make project-brain.json the sole mutable Project Brain state and keep documentation policy-only.
decisionLog.rationale: One validated artifact eliminates competing state authorities.
alternatives: Synchronize multiple hand-maintained Markdown records

positive: Runtime and project state share one source
negative: Human readers must inspect or render the canonical JSON

decisionLog.title: Allow only intent-based Project Brain mutations
decisionLog.context: Generic replacement could rewrite history or project identity.
decisionLog.decision: Remove public aggregate replacement and enforce identity and history at commit time.
decisionLog.rationale: Supported mutations must express domain intent and preserve auditability.
alternatives: Keep generic replacement with caller discipline

positive: Identity and append-only history are protected
negative: Each new mutation requires an explicit command

decisionLog.title: Use deterministic Blueprint Reader ports and parsers
decisionLog.context: BuilderAI must understand project documentation without coupling the domain to filesystems, frameworks, storage engines, or AI providers.
decisionLog.decision: Place discovery, parsing, validation, relationship analysis, consistency diagnostics, and summary generation in a framework-independent core behind a DocumentSource port; provide Node filesystem access as an infrastructure adapter.
decisionLog.rationale: Deterministic rules make project understanding portable, testable, and independent of AI and storage choices.
alternatives: Parse documents inside Next.js routes
Use an AI model to infer project structure
Couple discovery directly to Node filesystem APIs

positive: The reader can operate over memory, filesystems, or future sources without changing domain policy
Analysis is deterministic and testable
negative: Supported Markdown structure and version metadata must be explicit

decisionLog.title: Use one deterministic Context Package boundary
decisionLog.context: Downstream consumers need task-relevant project context without reading the entire repository or depending on a framework, storage engine, network service, or model integration.
decisionLog.decision: Build context through a pure core service that validates Project Brain and Blueprint Reader inputs, resolves explicit and lexical dependencies, applies a fixed priority order, enforces configurable limits, and emits one strongly typed Context Package.
decisionLog.rationale: A single validated and bounded package prevents consumers from bypassing governance, loading uncontrolled context, or interpreting competing context formats.
alternatives: Allow each downstream consumer to assemble repository context independently
Always load the entire project
Couple context assembly to a filesystem or application framework

positive: Context selection is deterministic, bounded, portable, and independently testable
Downstream consumers receive one validated contract
negative: Lexical relevance rules require explicit project vocabulary and relationship metadata
Very small limits may reject a package when mandatory governance context cannot fit

decisionLog.title: Use a closed provider-neutral adapter contract
decisionLog.context: Future providers must plug into BuilderAI without coupling the core to an SDK, transport, credentials, provider configuration, or execution workflow.
decisionLog.decision: Define a versioned core port with closed capability, Context Package request, response, configuration, validation, compatibility, registry, and typed error contracts; provide no production adapter or execution service.
decisionLog.rationale: A closed validated boundary preserves core independence, prevents provider-specific leakage, and makes discovery deterministic and testable without side effects.
alternatives: Import provider SDK abstractions into core services
Allow provider-specific dictionaries in configuration and payloads
Defer all contracts until selecting a provider

positive: Future adapters can implement one stable boundary without changing BuilderAI core
Provider discovery and compatibility remain deterministic, validated, and side-effect free
negative: A separately approved execution boundary is still required before any provider can run
Breaking contract changes require explicit versioning and migration

decisionLog.title: Insert one deterministic Prompt Package boundary
decisionLog.context: Future adapters need governed prompt material without independently formatting raw Context Packages or receiving duplicated task state.
decisionLog.decision: Transform each validated Context Package through a versioned provider-neutral template into one ordered, deduplicated, size-bounded Prompt Package; make that package the sole prompt-bearing object in provider requests.
decisionLog.rationale: A single structured boundary centralizes prompt policy, budgeting, safety, output expectations, and template evolution without provider coupling or execution.
alternatives: Allow every provider adapter to format Context Packages independently
Build provider-specific prompt strings in application services
Send the Context Package and duplicate task directly to providers

positive: Future providers receive one deterministic validated prompt contract
Prompt ordering, budgets, safety instructions, and output schemas remain provider independent
negative: The current schema omits only the complete optional Context section rather than granular items
Prompt quality and execution safety still require separate evaluation and approval

decisionLog.title: Use one pure append-only execution lifecycle
decisionLog.context: Future provider invocation needs deterministic coordination between the Prompt Package boundary and provider adapters without coupling core policy to queues, clocks, networks, SDKs, or provider behavior.
decisionLog.decision: Represent execution as a validated request and immutable versioned snapshot whose state changes only through a closed legal transition graph; keep retry and timeout as pure decisions, cancellation as a port contract, and results restricted to terminal snapshots.
decisionLog.rationale: An explicit append-only lifecycle centralizes orchestration invariants while leaving all runtime effects and provider invocation outside the core.
alternatives: Let each provider adapter own execution state and retry behavior
Use mutable status assignment without transition history
Introduce queues, timers, and provider invocation in the foundation

positive: Lifecycle, retry, timeout, cancellation, and terminal-result policy are deterministic and independently testable
Future runtime adapters cannot bypass validated identity and append-only transition evidence
negative: The foundation records decisions but does not schedule, wait, cancel, enforce deadlines, persist state, or invoke providers
Runtime idempotency, concurrency, recovery, and observability require a separately approved boundary

decisionLog.title: Isolate the first provider behind the OpenAI Responses adapter
decisionLog.context: BuilderAI needs to prove its provider-neutral Prompt Package, AIProvider, and Execution Engine boundaries with exactly one concrete integration.
decisionLog.decision: Implement openai-responses under src/providers/openai using the official SDK for one non-streaming Responses API call, explicit credential injection, deterministic request and response mapping, runtime output validation, stable error translation, and zero adapter or SDK retries.
decisionLog.rationale: Keeping all vendor behavior outside core proves the existing ports without coupling BuilderAI policy, lifecycle, or models to a provider SDK.
alternatives: Call the OpenAI REST API from core
Add OpenAI fields to provider-neutral contracts
Introduce multi-provider routing with the first integration

positive: Core contracts remain unchanged and provider independent
Requests and untrusted responses are validated at every boundary
The Execution Engine remains the owner of lifecycle and retry policy
negative: Production use still requires caller authorization, data classification, provider retention review, and a controlled live smoke test
Nested strict JSON Schema output requires a future versioned provider-neutral Output Contract

decisionLog.title: Insert one deterministic Response Package boundary
decisionLog.context: Validated provider output remains external, unordered data and Execution Results contain only artifact placeholders; future project-change workflows need one trustworthy, provider-independent response contract without receiving raw provider payloads or gaining side effects.
decisionLog.decision: Correlate one completed validated AIProviderResponse with its completed Execution Result, extract generated artifacts from one structured response artifact, normalize them deterministically, generate and verify an in-memory checksum manifest, and expose only one versioned Response Package from src/core/response-processor.
decisionLog.rationale: A single pure boundary centralizes response structure, closed artifact policy, size controls, canonical ordering, metadata rules, and integrity evidence while separating untrusted provider data from any future project mutation capability.
alternatives: Let future project writers consume provider responses directly
Place full generated file content inside the Execution Result placeholder contract
Generate manifests while writing artifacts to the filesystem

positive: Downstream consumers can depend on one provider-independent, deterministic, validated response contract
Artifact paths, types, metadata, byte sizes, and content checksums are verified before crossing the boundary
Response processing remains independently testable and performs no project-changing effect
negative: The current contract supports complete in-memory artifact content only and has configured aggregate limits
Checksums detect accidental or boundary drift but do not provide authenticity or signing
Applying, reviewing, authorizing, persisting, or rolling back artifacts requires a separately approved capability

decisionLog.title: Insert one effect-free Project Change Plan boundary
decisionLog.context: Response Packages contain deterministic artifacts but neither authorize project changes nor establish whether target paths exist; future review needs explicit operation intent, ordering, conflicts, provenance, and risk evidence without introducing project access or effects.
decisionLog.decision: Transform one validated Response Package into one versioned Project Change Plan under src/core/change-planner; require explicit Create File, Update File, or Delete File metadata, reject patch and ambiguous semantics, order operations create then update then delete by path, validate internal and source references, and always warn that current project-state preconditions are unverified.
decisionLog.rationale: A pure plan boundary makes proposed change intent deterministic and reviewable while keeping provider output interpretation, planning, current-state verification, authorization, and execution as separate trust boundaries.
alternatives: Inspect the filesystem to infer create and update operations
Let a future file writer interpret Response Packages directly
Model patch application, builds, tests, Git, and rollback in the planner

positive: Future reviewers receive one provider-independent, deterministic, conflict-checked change contract
Every operation preserves artifact checksum, size, type, description, package version, and execution provenance
The planner has no project-state or effect capability and cannot silently modify a repository
negative: Create, update, and delete existence preconditions remain unverified until a separately approved current-state boundary exists
Patch artifacts are rejected rather than interpreted
Application authorization, protected-path policy, content drift checks, atomic writes, isolated verification, Git, rollback, and audit remain future decisions

decisionLog.title: Apply file plans through one two-phase root-scoped boundary
decisionLog.context: Validated Project Change Plans are review evidence but BuilderAI needs a narrowly controlled filesystem effect boundary that prevents validation bypass, protected-path changes, symlink traversal, target races, and misleading multi-file outcomes without adding Git, process execution, networking, or rollback.
decisionLog.decision: Implement src/core/file-apply as a two-phase engine over root-scoped filesystem and clock ports; revalidate the complete plan, enforce mandatory and additional protected paths, inspect every target and create-parent before mutation, invoke only conditional create-if-absent, update-if-regular-file, and delete-if-regular-file methods, stop on first execution failure, and return an exact versioned Apply Result that distinguishes Rejected, Failed, Partially Applied, and Applied.
decisionLog.rationale: A single dependency-inverted effect boundary centralizes file safety policy and validation atomicity while making the absence of transactional rollback explicit and independently testable.
alternatives: Call Node filesystem APIs directly from orchestration
Let every workflow interpret and apply Change Plans independently
Implement transactional backup, rollback, Git, build, and test behavior in the first apply engine

positive: All rejectable plan and filesystem preconditions complete before the first mutation
Mandatory protected paths cannot be removed and filesystem implementations must contain paths and reject symlinks
Conditional mutation methods defend against target races after preflight
Actual partial outcomes remain visible instead of being reported as atomic success
negative: Multi-file application is not transactional and completed operations are not rolled back after a later failure
A production root-scoped filesystem adapter and operating-system conformance suite remain unimplemented
Expected-current-content checks, caller authorization, locking, recovery, reconciliation, audit, Git, build, test, deployment, and rollback remain separate decisions

decisionLog.title: Verify applied projects through one fixed evidence pipeline
decisionLog.context: A successful File Apply Result records completed file effects but does not prove that the resulting project, dependencies, build, or tests remain valid; verification needs controlled external execution without coupling core policy to a framework, process API, filesystem, network, or concrete runner.
decisionLog.decision: Implement src/core/verification as a fixed sequential Project Validation, Dependency Validation, Build Validation, and Test Validation pipeline; accept only a validated Applied File Apply Result, invoke each capability through its own port, validate and normalize every stage result, continue after contained stage failure, and derive one versioned report whose Passed, Failed, or Partially Passed status cannot drift from stage evidence.
decisionLog.rationale: A complete deterministic evidence report gives future workflows one trustworthy verification boundary while dependency inversion keeps privileged execution and framework choices outside core.
alternatives: Execute shell commands directly from the verification orchestrator
Stop at the first failed stage and omit remaining evidence
Allow arbitrary configured stages and adapter-defined overall status
Automatically repair failed verification

positive: Every accepted apply outcome receives the same complete ordered verification evidence
Malformed and thrown adapter outcomes are isolated as safe failed stages without leaking implementation details
Overall status, flattened findings, metadata, stage consistency, and ordering are independently runtime validated
Core remains framework, storage, filesystem, process, network, provider, and runner implementation independent
negative: All four stages run even after a failure, which favors evidence completeness over fail-fast execution cost
The fixed pipeline cannot add or omit stages without a versioned architectural change
Production runner adapters, sandboxing, command policy, active deadlines, process termination, output limits, authorization, and audit evidence remain unimplemented

decisionLog.title: Keep the first BuilderAI interface behind a fail-closed workflow port
decisionLog.context: BuilderAI needs a first user-facing dashboard and workspace, but the current architecture intentionally has no production filesystem or verification runner adapters and no authentication or authorization boundary for privileged project effects.
decisionLog.decision: Implement dashboard and project workspace routes under src/app and reusable client presentation under src/ui/workspace; load project facts through loadCanonicalProjectBrain, depend on existing response, plan, apply, and verification contracts through a typed WorkspaceWorkflowPort, require a separate review acknowledgement before apply, and ship the route in visible review mode when no authorized runtime port is composed.
decisionLog.rationale: A fail-closed presentation seam delivers and validates the complete human workflow without changing core business logic, inventing duplicate models, exposing credentials, fabricating success, or connecting an unauthenticated browser to privileged filesystem and process effects.
alternatives: Call core services and provider SDKs directly from browser components
Add unauthenticated server actions that execute live file and process adapters
Return hard-coded successful project results from a demo workflow
Delay every user interface until production runtime authorization exists

positive: Core modules and contracts remain unchanged and browser components have no privileged implementation dependency
Dashboard facts remain synchronized with canonical Project Brain state
Workflow transitions, explicit approval, safe failures, result views, responsive behavior, and accessibility can be tested deterministically
A future authorized server composition can implement the same UI port without rewriting the interface
negative: The shipped project workspace is review-only until an authorized runtime composition is separately approved
No end-to-end live provider, filesystem, build, or test action is available from the browser
Authentication, authorization, CSRF, idempotency, concurrency, audit, recovery, and hardened adapters remain prerequisites for live effects

decisionLog.title: Compose MVP v1.0 as a local-only server runtime
decisionLog.context: BuilderAI has validated core boundaries and a fail-closed workspace but needs an end-to-end MVP integration without adding authentication, persistence, deployment, rollback, multi-provider behavior, or new core capabilities.
decisionLog.decision: Compose existing services under src/application/workspace; expose bounded same-origin loopback route handlers; keep validated plans in a bounded expiring process-local store addressed by opaque identifiers; require explicit acknowledgement; apply only the server-held plan; provide root-scoped conditional Node filesystem effects and fixed shell-free bounded npm verification adapters outside core; and keep the runtime disabled when explicit server configuration is absent or invalid.
decisionLog.rationale: A local-only server composition completes the approved MVP workflow while preserving every core boundary, keeping secrets and privileged capabilities out of the browser, preventing plan substitution and duplicate application, and making unresolved hosted-runtime controls explicit rather than implied.
alternatives: Move provider, filesystem, or process behavior into client components
Accept the complete Project Change Plan back from the browser as effect authority
Add authentication, durable workflow persistence, sandbox infrastructure, and deployment beyond MVP scope
Leave the v1.0 workspace permanently disconnected

positive: The existing Project Brain through Verification pipeline is integrated without changing a core contract
Explicit approval is bound to an opaque server-held validated plan and completed outcomes replay idempotently
Provider credentials, SDK construction, filesystem access, process execution, and structured diagnostics remain server-only
Missing or invalid configuration preserves visible review mode
negative: The release is limited to a trusted local operator and trusted target project
Preparations are process-local and are lost on restart or unavailable across instances
Verification lacks OS sandboxing, guaranteed no-network enforcement, and complete process-tree isolation
Multi-file apply remains non-transactional without rollback, Git recovery, or durable audit storage

decisionLog.title: Add Gemini through the existing provider port
decisionLog.context: Local development needs Google AI Studio support without coupling core, UI, or application contracts to another provider SDK or removing OpenAI.
decisionLog.decision: Implement google-gemini under src/providers/gemini using the official SDK for one non-streaming structured request; select openai or gemini only in the server composition root through BUILDERAI_AI_PROVIDER and require only the selected provider configuration.
decisionLog.rationale: An isolated adapter and exhaustive composition branch extend local provider choice while preserving the provider-neutral contract, existing lifecycle policy, OpenAI behavior, and browser boundary.
alternatives: Replace OpenAI with Gemini
Add Gemini SDK and selection fields to core contracts
Build dynamic routing and provider fallback
Call Gemini directly from the UI

positive: OpenAI and Gemini remain interchangeable at the existing application port
Provider choice changes through server configuration only
Gemini credentials, SDK types, wire responses, and errors remain isolated and server-only
negative: A second SDK dependency and adapter require independent maintenance and audit review
Free-tier quota, regional availability, and provider data terms constrain local use
Provider switching requires a local server restart and has no automatic fallback

decisionLog.title: Implement baseline-guided surgical UPDATE contract (ADR-031)
decisionLog.context: Live smoke after ADR-030 showed providers frequently emit schema-valid full-file UPDATE_FILE rewrites for small modification requests. ADR-030 detects and surfaces preservation violations at plan time but does not inject baseline content or surgical intent into provider prompts.
decisionLog.decision: Add deterministic pre-generation surgical UPDATE behavior: HARD/SOFT/NONE update scope planning, PINNED_BASELINE admission for likely UPDATE targets, PRESERVATION_CONTRACT prompt section, correction preservation feedback derived from ADR-030 outputs, scope-deviation evidence on Change Plans, and compatibility with ADR-029 correction output bounding—without reversing ADR-017 full-file UPDATE semantics or ADR-030 post-generation preservation analysis.
decisionLog.rationale: Surgical modification of existing projects requires generation-quality improvement before provider execution while preserving Gate 2 human approval, provider-neutral orchestration, and unchanged ADR-030 safety signals.
alternatives: Prompt-only strengthening without guaranteed baseline in prompt
PATCH/diff artifacts violating ADR-017
Second-model scope planning
Auto-reject on elevated churn without operator review

positive: Provider receives authoritative CURRENT BASELINE for pinned UPDATE targets
Deterministic scope metadata (HARD/index.html/max-operations-1) verified on live smoke-atelier prepare
Correction loop consumes ADR-030 preservation evidence with bounded feedback
Scope discipline improved from multi-file rewrites to single-file surgical updates on representative task
negative: Prompt size increases for pinned baselines; lower-ranked context may be omitted
HARD scope heuristics may false-positive on narrow path patterns—mitigated by tests and fail-open NONE mode
Broader prompt-quality evaluation (injection resistance, secret scanning, regression corpus) remains separate pendingWork

decisionLog.title: Implement hybrid structured surgicality metrics for UPDATE_FILE (ADR-032)
decisionLog.context: ADR-031 Slice 4 live validation produced the mathematically minimal golden HTML accessibility patch at churnRatio=0.4444—unreachable under ADR-030 line-LCS GOOD (<0.40) despite zero structural or text changes and eight attribute-only edits. Gate 2 and correction feedback mis-classified exemplary patches as MARGINAL.
decisionLog.decision: Adopt Option C hybrid structured surgicality: keep ADR-030 line-LCS and Layer 1 preservation findings unchanged and authoritative; add deterministic parse5 HTML structuredAnalysis and SurgicalityClassifierService; when parseStatus=SUCCESS use STRUCTURED_HTML surgicality for Gate 2 and correction feedback with line churn diagnostic only; retain GENERIC_LINE_LCS fallback for JS/CSS/non-HTML and parser fallback.
decisionLog.rationale: Metric semantics must align with surgical intent without weakening ADR-030 preservation safety or changing churn formulas/thresholds.
alternatives: Character-ratio surgicality alone
Threshold-only adjustment raising GOOD above 0.4444
Minimum-delta normalization requiring task semantics
Suppressing PRESERVATION_ELEVATED_CHURN for structured EXCELLENT

positive: Golden smoke-atelier patch classified EXCELLENT/STRUCTURED_HTML with 8/0/0 structured delta
Gate 2 displays structured surgicality and line metrics together with GATE_2_ACCEPT_RECOMMENDED
Correction feedback prioritizes stable IDs, text, structure, and attribute delta—not churn targets—for HTML
964 tests pass; ADR-030 regression preserved
negative: Operators may see EXCELLENT surgicality alongside PRESERVATION_ELEVATED_CHURN until optional UI polish
Live correction prepare end-to-end re-validation deferred due to provider timeout—non-blocking
parse5 dependency added for HTML analysis only

decisionLog.title: External target workspace project profile (ADR-0033)
decisionLog.context: Trusted-local workspace prepare required BuilderAI's full governance document stack on every target repository, blocking onboarding for existing applications such as Zyro.lk with PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID before useful development.
decisionLog.decision: Add BUILDERAI_WORKSPACE_PROJECT_PROFILE with BUILDERAI_SELF (default, unchanged strict Blueprint Reader validation) and EXTERNAL_TARGET (minimal bootstrap contract: .builderai/target-project.json, docs/architecture.md, docs/project-constitution.md, docs/ai-rules.md, package.json). Fail closed with EXTERNAL_TARGET_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED when bootstrap context is missing.
decisionLog.rationale: Separate BuilderAI self-governance from external application onboarding without disabling project validation or filesystem, authorization, or apply protections.
alternatives: Disable PROJECT_VALIDATION for external repos
Require full BuilderAI governance stack in every target repository
Implicit profile detection without explicit operator configuration

positive: Existing application repositories can onboard in under one hour with four bootstrap files
BuilderAI repository strict validation remains default
Context builder receives architecture, constitution, and ai-rules from target-owned docs
negative: Operators must set BUILDERAI_WORKSPACE_PROJECT_PROFILE explicitly for external targets
Full-stack indexing and hosted production onboarding remain future checkpoints

progressLog.currentMilestone: BUILDERAI_ZYROLK_READY complete: trusted-local single-operator development for external targets (e.g. Zyro.lk) with Gate 2 review, full-stack context, operator UX, and Zyro-aligned verification. Boundary: trusted-local only — not hosted production or unattended autonomy.
